newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: IASA seeks Latam, M. East members.
newsitem.headline: IASA seeks Latam, M. East members.

text.p: The International Air Shipping Association(IASA) plans to expand its network in Latin America and the Middle East, IASA chief executive, Philip Turner told Reuter.
Argentina, Brazil, Chile and Mexico will be tarqeted by the organisation initially, he said

IASA is a worldwide network of independent airfreight forwarders which has been in existence for 25 years. The association was established in 1971 in Amsterdam and now has 40 members in its global network.
IASA's secretariat is currently based at London Heathrow, while its sales and marketing office is at Schiphol airport.
However, in the next few years the group will probably move all of its operations to London. Labour costs and very strict Dutch labour laws are the major reasons for the move, added Turner
In Europe, Finland, Sweden and some eastern European countries will also be targeted by TASA.
Turner said that new members from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Bahrain joined at IASA's recent annual general meeting in Manila and it hoping to attract members from Jordan, Lebanon and Yemen.

The AGM, attended by 55 delegates from 32 countries, also saw the appointment of a new president and chairman, Edward Byrne from Ireland's Byrne Air Freight, who will hold the post for the next two years.
In addition, the agents' network is looking for agents in the U.S. midwest region, Chicago/Detroit region, and Florida.
IASA members total exports revenue -- based on International Air Transport Association (IATA)data -- was U.S. $450m last year and around 2,500 people work in the organisation, he said.
Turner added that IASA is keen to raise its profile. "We are known by most of the airlines but not necessarily the shippers." ---Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
